inventory_boundary.reason: The fresh-context phase-1 inventory is the authoritative atomic denominator: 57 numeric claims plus one nonnumeric circuit schematic. The paired reviewer submission adjudicates every numeric claim.
inventory_boundary.next_action: Keep the 58-row inventory frozen. W2 work is limited to the three explicitly uncovered numeric claims R046, R053, and R054.

acceptance_criteria: Direct dephasing minimization matches the closed formula.
Classical-quantum states satisfy the commutator and rank criteria.
All formula-defined Fig. 1 domains and extrema are generated.
DQC1 trace, separability, and classicality identities pass.
The subsystem-versus-rest criterion works for 2-8 parties and local dimensions 2-5, with exact basis-search dimensions frozen.
The reconstructed multipartite optimizer recovers rotated classical, GHZ, and maximally entangled qudit analytic references.
The paper's local prepare/reset examples create and remove discord without using source pixels.
The runner reads no raw source, author code, author arrays, or source pixels.
The phase-times-involution normalized-trace identity passes direct matrix cross-checks.
Missing circuit-family, approximation, classical-model, and reduction fields remain explicit rather than guessed.
The runner reads no raw source, author code, author arrays, or source pixels.
Every unique bipartition with the control fixed on side A is enumerated.
The analytic control-versus-register separability limit has zero negativity.
The chosen negativity proxy and all paper-omitted conventions remain explicit.
The runner reads no raw source, author code, author arrays, or source pixels.

items.scientific_object: DQC1 Hadamard, controlled-U, and control-measurement circuit drawing.
items.paper_assertion: Figure 2 schematically depicts the DQC1 circuit.
items.reason: The circuit topology is nonnumeric; its quantitative consequences are inventoried separately as R039-R043 and R045-R054.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Quantum mutual-information identity.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: I(rho)=H(rho_A)+H(rho_B)-H(rho).
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh review supports the independently checked identity.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: POVM-optimized classical-correlation definition.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Q_A=H(rho_B)-min sum_k p_k H(rho_{B|k}).
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh review supports the independently checked definition.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: One-sided quantum-discord definition.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: D_A=I-Q_A.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh review supports the identity.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Nonnegativity and exact classical-state zero of D_A.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: D_A is nonnegative and vanishes for classically correlated states.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent exact and regression checks support the claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Normalization, positivity, and separability of the displayed two-qubit state.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Eq. (4) is a normalized separable density state.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh review and independent matrix construction support all three properties.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Nonzero left discord of the separable Eq. (4) state.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The Eq. (4) state has non-vanishing left discord.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh review applies a basis-independent zero-discord criterion.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Measurement-invariance characterization of zero discord.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: D_A=0 iff a rank-one local measurement on A leaves rho invariant.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh review supports both directions.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Classical-quantum decomposition of zero-left-discord states.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Zero-left-discord states have the orthogonal-label decomposition printed in the paper.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh review supports the equivalence.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Real correlation-matrix expansion in local Hermitian bases.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Every bipartite state has the printed real R expansion.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent reconstruction supports the expansion.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Operator-Schmidt SVD and rank identity.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: SVD of R gives L=rank(R) nonzero operator-Schmidt terms.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent rank/reconstruction checks support the claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Coefficientwise measurement invariance of nonzero Schmidt operators.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: rho invariance is equivalent to invariance of each nonzero S_n.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh proof and exact-rank tests support the claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Pairwise-commutation criterion for zero left discord.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: D_A=0 iff all left Schmidt operators commute pairwise.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent commutator and structure checks support the criterion.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Unordered-pair commutator count.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: At most L(L-1)/2 commutators must be checked.
quantitative_claims.reason: Exact pair enumeration supports the count.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Rectangular correlation-matrix rank bound.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: L<=min(d_A^2,d_B^2).
quantitative_claims.reason: Linear-algebra audit supports the bound.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Operator-Schmidt rank bound for classical-quantum states.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Every zero-left-discord state has L<=d_A.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh proof and exact examples support the bound.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Rank witness for nonzero left discord.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: L>d_A suffices to witness nonzero left discord.
quantitative_claims.reason: Contrapositive and physical-state checks support the witness.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Partial-correlation-matrix rank certification without tomography.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: d_A+1 independent measured rows/columns certify nonzero discord.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent rank construction supports the certification rule.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Hilbert-Schmidt geometric-discord definition.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: D_A^(2)=min_{chi in Omega_0} Tr[(rho-chi)^2].
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh minimization audit supports the definition.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Complete two-qubit Bloch representation.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Every two-qubit state has the printed x,y,T Pauli expansion.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent reconstruction supports the representation.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Unit Bloch vector of a pure basis state.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: e=<psi_1|sigma|psi_1> and ||e||=1.
quantitative_claims.reason: Exact Pauli checks support the identity.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Conditional Bloch-vector definitions s_plus/minus.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: s_plus/minus equal the printed weighted conditional Pauli traces.
quantitative_claims.reason: Direct matrix evaluation supports the identity.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Bloch triple and parameter bounds for zero-left-discord states.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: A zero-left-discord state has {t e,s_plus,e s_minus^T} with the printed bounds.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh structure and norm checks support the parameterization.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Expanded Hilbert-Schmidt distance objective.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: ||rho-chi||^2 equals the displayed quadratic function.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent algebra supports the expansion.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Strict convexity and unique fixed-e minimum.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The fixed-e objective has positive nonsingular Hessian and a unique global minimum.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent Hessian calculation supports the claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Stationary solution t=x dot e.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Stationarity gives t=x dot e.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent differentiation supports the equation.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Stationary solution s_plus=y.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Stationarity gives s_plus=y.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent differentiation supports the equation.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Stationary solution s_minus=T^T e.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Stationarity gives s_minus=T^T e.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent differentiation supports the equation.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Feasibility bounds for the stationary point.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: |x dot e|, ||y||, and ||T^T e|| are at most one.
quantitative_claims.reason: State-positivity and norm checks support the bounds.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Closed two-qubit geometric-discord formula.
quantitative_claims.reason: Direct minimization and eigenvalue checks support the formula.

quantitative_claims.source_ref: Maximally mixed marginals paragraph and Fig. 1, p. 3
quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Local-unitary Bell-diagonal canonical form.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Every two-qubit state with maximally mixed marginals is LU-equivalent to rho(t).
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh analytic review and generated geometry support the claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Physical Bell-diagonal tetrahedron and its four vertices.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Physical t-vectors form the printed tetrahedron.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent eigenvalue constraints support the tetrahedron.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Separable Bell-diagonal octahedron and its six vertices.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Separable t-vectors form the printed octahedron.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent PPT constraints support the octahedron.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Bell-diagonal specialization of geometric discord.
quantitative_claims.reason: Formula substitution and generated geometry support the claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Zero-discord coordinate-axis line segments.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Bell-diagonal discord vanishes exactly when at most one t_i is nonzero.
quantitative_claims.reason: Exact formula and geometry checks support the axes.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Global Bell-state maximum of geometric discord.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The global maximum is 1/2 at the tetrahedron vertices.
quantitative_claims.reason: Exact constrained evaluation supports the Bell-state maximum.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Separable-domain maximum and maximizer locations.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The separable maximum is 1/6 at all eight facet centers.
quantitative_claims.reason: Exact rederivation and independent enumeration reproduce a stable contradiction: facet centers give 1/18 and edge midpoints maximize at 1/16.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Index-generated family of separable-discord maximizers.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: i_k=plus/minus1 in (-1)^{i_k} generates eight distinct states.
quantitative_claims.reason: Exact exponent enumeration validates the paper-error candidate: the literal domain collapses to one matrix.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Swap symmetry and equality of left/right discord for the intended Eq. (17) family.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The intended family is swap-symmetric and D_A=D_B.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent matrix symmetry checks support the claim after separating the R037 typo.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Normalized DQC1 input state.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The control is (I+alpha sigma_3)/2 and register I/2^n.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent density-matrix checks support the input.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Exact DQC1 output density matrix.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The circuit output equals the printed block expression.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent circuit/block-matrix derivation supports the output.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Loss of trace signal at alpha=0.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: At alpha=0 the output is completely mixed and carries no trace-task signal.
quantitative_claims.reason: Exact limit check supports the claim.

quantitative_claims.source_ref: Fig. 2 caption and after Eq. (18), pp. 3-4
quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Control Pauli readout of normalized trace.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: sigma_1/sigma_2 means yield Re/Im Tr(U)/2^n.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent trace identities support the readout.

quantitative_claims.source_ref: Fig. 2 caption and after Eq. (18), pp. 3-4
quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Sampling overhead scaling with control polarization.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Normalized-trace sampling overhead scales as 1/alpha^2.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent variance/error scaling supports the claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Control-versus-register separability of DQC1 output.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The control qubit is completely separable from the register.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh analytic decomposition supports the split.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Entanglement across every split grouping control with register qubits and its n-scaling.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Entanglement is vanishingly small across all such regrouped bipartitions.
quantitative_claims.reason: All regrouped splits now have runnable negativity code and attested finite-size data, but the paper supplies no entanglement measure, smallness threshold, unitary ensemble, or asymptotic rate, so the paper claim remains scientifically underdetermined.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Generic nonzero discord for Haar-random U.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Almost every random U produces non-vanishing left discord.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh measure-zero argument and independent sampling support the claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Equivalence of Eq. (18) and sigma_1/sigma_2 decomposition.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Eq. (18) equals the printed Eq. (19) decomposition.
quantitative_claims.reason: Direct matrix expansion supports the identity.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Linear-dependence criterion for zero DQC1 discord.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: At alpha nonzero, zero discord iff Hermitian and anti-Hermitian parts of U are linearly dependent.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent commutator analysis supports the equivalence.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Scalar-adjoint form of the DQC1 zero-discord condition.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Linear dependence is equivalent to U^dagger=kU.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh algebra supports the equivalence.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Phase-times-involution characterization.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: U^dagger=kU iff U=e^{i phi}A with A^2=I.
quantitative_claims.reason: Spectral derivation and matrix checks support the characterization.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Classicality of all correlations for phase-times-involution U.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: For U=e^{i phi}A with A^2=I, all DQC1 output correlations are classical.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent zero-discord structure checks support the claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Classical hardness of normalized trace for zero-discord phase-times-involution instances.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The task remains classically hard because A may have complex eigenvectors.
quantitative_claims.reason: The executable boundary verifies that the normalized trace depends only on the phase and +/-1 multiplicities, but no input encoding, approximation tolerance, classical model, or reduction is specified, so hardness remains unproved.

quantitative_claims.source_ref: Abstract and final DQC1 paragraph, pp. 1 and 4
quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Resource conclusion excluding discord as the cause of DQC1 speedup.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: Quantum discord is unlikely to be the resource responsible for DQC1 speedup.
quantitative_claims.reason: The algebraic zero-discord family and its trace identity are executable, but the resource conclusion still depends on the unresolved R053 hardness premise.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Nonmonotonicity of Hilbert-Schmidt geometric discord under local operations.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: D_A^(2) is not monotonic under local operations.
quantitative_claims.reason: Independent prepare/reset channels support both directions of nonmonotonicity.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Normalization of the written zero-discord input operator.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: |00><00|+|11><11| is a density state.
quantitative_claims.reason: Exact trace evaluation and independent channel construction validate a missing factor 1/2 in the printed state.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Discord creation by mapping orthogonal labels to nonorthogonal states.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The local map converts the normalized zero-discord input into nonzero discord.
quantitative_claims.reason: A valid measure-and-prepare channel and independent commutator/dephasing checks support the intended claim.

quantitative_claims.scientific_object: Multipartite extension and scaling of criterion/evaluation difficulty.
quantitative_claims.paper_assertion: The method extends to any number of subsystems while evaluation becomes harder with count and dimension.
quantitative_claims.reason: Fresh review and independently generated multipartite scaling/optimizer evidence support the extension.
